L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Ipratropium, a quaternary ammonium alkaloid, has absolute oral bioavailability of 2.3% (10 mg), 2.0% (2 mg), and 3.27% (20 mg) in healthy volunteers, demonstrating very low F for a permanently charged ammonium compound.
Physostigmine, an N-methyl indoline alkaloid, has oral bioavailability of 1-5%, with a mean absolute bioavailability of 3% for an oral solution, well below the 20% threshold.
Lisuride, an ergoline alkaloid, has oral bioavailability of about 10% after a 100 µg oral dose, below the 20% threshold.
Pentazocine mean oral bioavailability is 18% from 100 mg tablets, below the 20% threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental bioavailability measurement is available for the query molecule.
The explicit [N@+] quaternary ammonium in the SMILES conflicts with the computed neutral fraction of 0.98; if the permanent cation is real, the favorable logD/TPSA-based prior is not reliable.
Transfer from ipratropium and physostigmine is analog-based; species, formulation, and dose differences could alter absolute bioavailability.

A few context records show values above 20% (nitrendipine 30%, pentazocine individual 31.6%, physostigmine 23%), but these are less structurally relevant or are outliers within otherwise low-F datasets.

The physicochemical high-F prior is undermined by the explicit permanent cation. Confidence is moderate because no direct query-specific bioavailability data are available.
